sections.content: How many people stayed in Solihull after gaining qualifications?

Solihull is a large town in the West Midlands. Solihull does not have its own university.

Solihull has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Solihull ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 6,055 state-school pupils from Solihull who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,920 (48%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,865 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Solihull to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Solihull's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Solihull in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Solihull move to?

Of Solihull's graduates, 1,020 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 270 of those graduates (26%) were living fairly locally, in the Birmingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Solihull's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 555 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 345 of those qualified non-graduates (62%) were living fairly locally, in the Birmingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Solihull's GCSE cohort:

  • 665 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 150 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 18% of graduates and 20% of qualified non-graduates living in Solihull had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,265 graduates and 1,595 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Solihull. This is compared with the 2,920 graduates and 1,865 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 82% of the graduates had also lived in Solihull as GCSE pupils, while 18% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Solihull in 2018 to 2019, 80% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 20% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
